subject: Sequenced onboarding activation matrix and API contract alignment
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@valiantbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@valiantbank.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up — onboarding approach + timeline questions

Karthik,

Thanks for the RFP response so far. The procurement team reviewed the high-level approach and asked for a concrete sequenced activation plan we can take to our ops and security teams. Specifically can you provide:

- A week-by-week timeline for a 10-week onboarding (discovery -> prod), called out by milestone (API integration, data schema handshake, QA canary, full ramp).
- The canary cadence (cohort sizes, success gates, rollback criteria).
- The API contract items we should pin for the integration sprint (headers, auth, rate limits, error codes, idempotency expectations).
- Any prerequisites from our side (network egress, certs, IP allowlist, test data).

We'd like a short document/attachment we can circulate to our architecture and security leads. Also include any draft contract language that affects go-live (SLA, data handling).

Can you get something to us by EOD Wednesday PT?

Thanks,
Jared
Director, Platform Engineering
Valiant Bank
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@valiantbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — onboarding approach + timeline questions

Jared — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise activation matrix and a high-level runbook (activation_matrix_v2.xlsx; redwood_onboarding_runbook.pdf). Below is the sequenced plan we recommend; I also pasted the key API contract bullets at the end.

Summary plan (10-week timeline, weeks numbered):
- Weeks 1–2 (Discovery & kickoff): access provisioning, network verification (IP allowlist), share test schema, auth key exchange.
- Weeks 3–4 (Integration sprint): implement API client, map fields, automated contract tests against our sandbox.
- Week 5 (Pre-canary verification): end-to-end test, latency/load baseline, run integration smoke tests.
- Weeks 6–7 (Canary cohort staging): 3-step canary (1% -> 5% -> 20%), each stage runs with defined success gates.
- Week 8 (Ramp to steady-state): 50% traffic for 48–72h, monitor quality/regressions.
- Weeks 9–10 (Final cutover & hypercare): full production routing, rollback window, runbook handoff to your SREs.

Canary cadence & success gates (recommended):
- Cohort A: 1% traffic for 48 hours. Gates: error rate < 0.5% above baseline; 95th p50/p95 latency within agreed SLO; no data integrity exceptions.
- Cohort B: 5% traffic for 72 hours. Gates: same thresholds + model output quality check against seeded prompt set (pass rate >= 95%).
- Cohort C: 20% traffic for 72 hours. Gates: stability maintained; auto-scale behavior validated.

Rollback criteria (examples):
- Sustained error rate > 1% for 30 minutes, or a quality degradation delta > 8% vs baseline on seeded prompts.
- Any data leakage/security finding from the compliance checklist.

Key API contract items to pin in the sprint:
- Auth: OAuth2 bearer tokens; token rotation window (30d) and rotation endpoint.
- Rate limits: vendor default 60 rps per route; request-level rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining). We will provide negotiated baseline for your Dedicated pool.
- Error model: structured error body with code, message, request_id. 429 and 503 semantics must be respected; clients should implement exponential backoff.
- Idempotency: POST operations that mutate must accept an Idempotency-Key header.

Prerequisites for Valiant:
- Allowlist our outbound IPs (list in runbook), establish mTLS or TLS with certs as required, provide a test dataset (anonymized) for quality checks.

Attachments: activation_matrix_v2.xlsx (detailed week-by-week checklist), redwood_onboarding_runbook.pdf (runbook + IP list). Also attached an initial API contract draft (api_contract_draft.docx).

I'll set up a 60-minute working session tomorrow to walk through the matrix unless you prefer a different time.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@valiantbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@valiantbank.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — onboarding approach + timeline questions

Thanks Karthik — the matrix looks useful. A couple of clarifications from our side that will affect canary sizing and the schedule:

1) Data residency: our legal team requires that production inference for US customers remains in our US-only VPC peering setup. Can you confirm routing options and whether we can pin region and Dedicated capacity?
2) SLA baseline: we need an initial target SLO for latency (p95 < 250ms) and an availability SLA to include in the term sheet.
3) Compliance evidence: do you have current SOC 2 type II date/range and a SOC report we can share?

Also, our security manager wants the exact list of artifacts you hand over in the final runbook (audit logs, KV cache handling notes, encryption-at-rest keys info).

If we can get those answers before the working session that would be ideal.

—Jared
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@valiantbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@valiantbank.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — onboarding approach + timeline questions

Hi Jared — looping in quick answers from the security & compliance side.

1) Regional routing & Dedicated capacity: Yes — we can pin Dedicated capacity to a US region and route by policy. Our Private deployment option also supports VPC peering. I'll include a diagram in the runbook showing peering and network flows.

2) SLA baseline: For Dedicated customers we can contract an availability SLA (example 99.9%) and an inferred latency SLO target; typical p95 for enterprise models on Dedicated at medium sequence lengths is ~180–220ms. We'll propose p95 < 250ms in the draft SLA and include an escalation path.

3) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II audit covering 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31. We'll provide the report under an NDA.

Artifacts handed over at cutover (examples):
- Audit logs (access and request logs) retention policy and export procedures
- KV cache behavior and warming notes
- Key management notes (KMS integration points; we do not ship keys)
- Endpoint allowlist & cert fingerprints
- Canary monitoring dashboards and runbook playbook with rollback steps

I'll also add security contacts and expected evidence timelines to the runbook (attaching an addendum in the Drive link).

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@valiantbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: integration@valiantbank.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — onboarding approach + timeline questions

Jared — quick technical notes on rollout mechanics and fallback behavior that will be part of the runbook:

- Autoscale & burst: Dedicated pools support configured autoscaling up to a burst cap. We'll set the initial autoscale policy to +30% above baseline traffic for the first 72h of ramp, then tune.
- Model variants & graceful degradation: we support on-the-fly fallback to a quantized (lower-cost) variant that preserves API contract; fallback is controlled by policy and is automatic if latency or memory pressure thresholds exceed safe levels. We'll provide the exact thresholds and a toggle in the console.
- Monitoring & observability: token-level cost breakdown, request_id tracing, per-route latency histograms, and a canary checklist that emits events to your PagerDuty integration.
- Contract draft note: api_contract_draft.docx includes the expected error codes, idempotency behavior, and the headers we'll require for tracing. Please review and mark redlines in the Docx; we'll prepare a clean contract to attach to the MSA.

I'll be on the session and can walk through the fallback policy controls.

—Markus
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks — Jared
